utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-75-T, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President and Your Honours. Douglas Stringer, Alex Demirdjian, Uros Zigic, and Case Manager Thomas Laugel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Zoran Zivanovic and Christopher Gosnell for the Defence of Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we bring the witness in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you for coming today to assist us with your testimony. First of all, do you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Judge Delvoie's microphone please be switched on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I'm very sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rakic, Gorana.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And your date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 12th of November, 1956.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am a Serb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. You are about to read the solemn declaration by which witnesses commit themselves to tell the truth. I have to point out that that solemn declaration that you are about to make does expose you to the penalty of perjury should you give untruthful or misleading information to this Tribunal. Could you now please read the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Rakic. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Your witness, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Rakic.

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I will be asking you first a few questions about your statement, and if you require any clarifications, don't hesitate to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we display on the screen 65 ter 2379, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Rakic, it is correct to say that you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in May of 1999?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And that this statement was written in the English language and was read back to you in the Serbian language before you signed?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you see this statement before you now?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And at the bottom of the English version do you see your signature?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And it is correct to say that you signed every page of this statement?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: When you arrived in The Hague a few days ago, you were given a copy of this statement translated in your language; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: When you reviewed your statement I believe you had a correction to one of the sentences; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we go there now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It's at page 3 of both English and B/C/S versions. And could we zoom into the top part, the very first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And I would like to take your attention to the last sentence of that very first paragraph which I believe begins with, "I am sure that my husband would get a weapon ..." Could you tell the Court what is the clarification you would like to make to this part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as the statement is concerned, the one that was drafted -- or, rather, translated, "I am sure that my husband would get a weapon if there were weapon distributions in the village," my correction is that my husband certainly would not have taken a weapon and brought it home with him because we both disliked weapons and didn't want to have any weapons in our house, either earlier on or subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Putting aside this sentence that you have now clarified for the Trial Chamber, is the rest of your statement accurate?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And with regards to the answers that are recorded in your statement, would you give the same answers in the court should you be asked the same questions?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I ask to admit -- tender this statement, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it shall be assigned Exhibit P272. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Ms. Rakic, I will now ask you additional questions relating to topics that are contained in your statement. First of all, in your statement you indicate that you worked for banks in Osijek. Could you explain to the Trial Chamber what was your educational background?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I completed secondary school, secondary school for economics. I worked in a bank in Osijek for 13 years. I started as a trainee, and by 1990, I was in charge of the shift -- of a shift. I supervised 20 employees. So I was, in fact, a supervisor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now in your statement - and I will skip in time a little bit - you explained the situation in the summer of 1991 and at the top of page 3 you explain that you left Erdut on the 20th of July, 1991, and that you stayed with your aunt in Serbia. Could you tell the Court when you returned from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I returned on the 19th of August, 1991, from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And upon your return, did you -- did you resume working?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: You mean in Osijek? No, of course not. I returned to the village, and since the JNA was already in the village at the time we had an obligation - I don't know how else to put it - to perform work duties in the village. Everyone had to perform certain duties on the basis of what one had previously done in accordance with one's previous profession.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what work obligation were you assigned to?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I was assigned work in the TO staff, the Territorial Defence Staff, and I had to work as an accountant in that staff. It involved the work that was performed in the canteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And before doing this work as an accountant, is it correct to say that you were also involved in the cleaning or the organising of the TO centre?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I personally wasn't involved in that. I was expecting the work of an accountant, but other people who were there, other women who were there did perform such work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you explain to the Trial Chamber what was your role or your function as an accountant? What did you have to do on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I had to do the following. As I have already said, it -- it was a certain position that had to do with -- with the economy. I had to make a list of the various goods, various items needed for the canteen, cooking items for the employees there. Items for people who were cleaning the centre, items for the employees who worked in the vineyards and picked grapes. So I had to make a list of all the various goods that were needed and procured by that centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. You explain in your statement that your superior or your boss was a man by the name of Dragomir Lastavica from Dalj; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to show you now an image of this area, and if you could estimate to us the various locations of your offices, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we explain 65 ter 6254. That's at tab 21. Is that not on e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Ms. Rakic, we will return to this in a moment. It appears that we are having some technical problems with the image. I will skip to my next set of questions. Now you explain in your statement that Arkan arrived in September 1991 and that he came to your office and introduced himself. Could you tell the Court how did he introduce himself exactly?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: He entered the office. He very calmly introduced himself. He said he was the leader of the Serbian Volunteer Guards. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And when he arrived at the training centre -- well, when you saw him on that day, where was he stationed following this introduction?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: At the time he was stationed in that centre, in the Territorial Defence centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And was -- you explain in your statement that he arrived with around 30 men. Was there a guard at the entrance of the training centre?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I think there were men from the JNA reserve forces there prior to his arrival.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And were they still there after his arrival?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: No. The army withdrew to the premises of the primary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You also mentioned a man by the name of Radovan Stojicic in your statement and that you saw him in Erdut. I'd like to ask you if you saw him at the training centre.

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I think I saw him on a number of occasions. On a couple of occasions he came to attempt to reach certain agreements, something of that sort. But in any event he did go to the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And when he came to the centre, did you know who he came to meet with?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In your statement you say that he was stationed at the Saponija facility. Can you tell us what the distance is between this facility and the training centre?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: It's very close as the crow flies. I think it would be between 800 metres and 1 kilometre. In fact, 800 metres between the Saponija facility and the Territorial Defence centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. In relation to the logistic aspects of the TO centre's operation, I want you to look at a document that's going to appear on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Its 65 ter 00445. That's at tab 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Ms. Rakic, this is a military document that's in front of your screen. It is correct to say that you have never seen this document before, right?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'd like you to help us with some of the information included in this report. In the very first paragraph it indicates that 30 members of the Serb national guard under the command of Arkan are based in the training centre. Now does that match with the information that you had at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether there were 20, the 25, 30, or 35 of them exactly, but roughly speaking, yes, that's how many of them there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In the next paragraph it is indicated that the centre had a capacity of 270 beds. Now, I'm pretty sure you never had to count those beds but where would those be located?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Well, I assume beds and what we used to call a hotel -- well, they were dormitories before the 1990s there for JNA reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And when you say "dormitories," do I understand this was part of the centre itself in the compound?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In the next paragraph we see that in keeping with Arkan's order, 19 women from the village of Erdut were currently employed in the centre. Can you tell us if this matches with the information you had at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether there were 19 of them. I think there were fewer of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What was the information you had at the time in terms of numbers? We don't have to be precise, but roughly, if you know.

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps there were up to ten of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The next sentence indicates that Arkan ordered a local TO to provide transportation to work and back for these women. Was this something that you were aware about?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. The next paragraph indicates some of the equipment available at the centre, large quantities of infantry weapons, and there is a discussion about a huge warehouse. Did you personally see a huge warehouse with weapons?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you see Arkan and his men training at the training centre?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I didn't see them in the centre itself, but they would wander around, walk around the streets with their weapons and with --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: What the witness calls "phantoms on their heads."

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you explain what the word "phantoms" means?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: They were caps, woollen caps, with slits for their eyes and for their mouth. Probably balaclavas. Ski masks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And just to be clear, you said earlier that they would walk around the streets. I assume you mean of the town of Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said. I would see them in the streets of Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And how frequently would you see them in the streets of Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Sometimes in the morning and in the afternoon. In the course of one day, I don't know how often. In fact, quite a lot of time has passed since then. But at least once a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could we go to the next page, please. This is the last page of this two-page document. And if we could zoom into the bottom part.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In the paragraph before the last one, there is a description of the reaction of the inhabitants of the village of Erdut. And the last sentence describes that the presence of Arkan in the centre and his conduct causes great discontent. Is this something that you witnessed at the time, the reaction of the inhabitants of Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Well, I assume that their reactions were the same as mine, because when you see that a group of 20 men are walking around with ski masks on their heads and with weapons, well, that does not leave you indifferent. You get out of their way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P273. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I am informed that the aerial image is now available. Can we go back to 65 ter 6254, please, tab 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Ms. Rakic, we are going to have the aerial image on the screen now. And with the assistance of the usher I would like you to mark certain areas. Yes. Do you recognise this image, Ms. Rakic?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: This photograph is an aerial photograph of the Territorial Defence centre. There is the new winery which is part of the IPK, and there is the old part of the chateau which is also part of the IPK, the industrial and agricultural enterprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can the usher please help the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Ms. Rakic, could you, first of all, with the pen that will be provided to you in a moment, indicate where was the gate or the entrance of the training centre and these grounds that we see here? You can mark it with a number 1.

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It's not very easy. You could try again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we erase it, Mr. Usher?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The usher will now erase it so you can try again. If you could put a number 1 and put a circle around it, if that makes it easier.

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now to -- can you indicate to us where your office was when you started to work in August of 1991 as an accountant?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to mark it and put number 2 next to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what is this building that we see now. We see that you marked as number 2 this very long building. What else was there in this building?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: The kitchen of the centre for Territorial Defence training and the mess, the dining room.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Could you mark that area with a number 3.

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Earlier we discussed this hotel or dormitories. Where would those be located?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And next to the building that you marked with a number 4 there seems to be another building. What was that used for?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now did your office -- was your office always located at the same place throughout the time that you worked at the training centre?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: No, no. I believe that in the month of September, sometime in mid-September, I moved to an office which was part of the IPK compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Is that visible on this image?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let's mark that with a number 5, please.

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what caused you to move from one office to the other?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Arkan had taken over the entire centre. He had his - I don't know what to call her - a woman who performed all sorts of duties for him, his correspondence and everything else. So she took my old office and I moved together with Mr. Lastavica. We both moved to the old chateau, the old manor, which at that time housed the administrative offices of the IPK.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You told us earlier that Arkan was stationed here. Which area did he move into with his men?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: What do you mean when you ask me where he moved to?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You told us earlier that when Arkan introduced himself to you, following that he was stationed at the TO training centre. On this image which area of -- which area was it that he occupied with his men?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I marked it and put number 4 next to it. He used those as his dormitory and he used number 3 as his dining room.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And could you tell us where were the offices of the government at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Shall I also mark it with a number?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, please. Yeah, with number 6.

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I believe that they were here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And the building that you marked with a number 5, we see this long yellowish building, was it referred to in some way? Did it have a name, this building?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: It's the old manor. It used to belong to Count Damovic in the past.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And when we talk about the winery generally, which area of this compound was referred to as the winery in 1991?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I'll put number 7 next to the new winery which was built before the 1990s. It is still operational. Next to that new building they also used -- and I will mark that with number 8. In the old part of the IPK, which was also one part of the Damovic manor, and that's where the old cellars were and there was also a collection of wines there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And when you say -- oh, yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, can we freeze this image and I would like to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter document 6254, marked by the witness in court, shall be assigned Exhibit P274. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now at page -- I'm moving now to a different topic, Ms. Rakic. At page 4 of your statement you were mentioning about Hungarians who had been brought to the training centre in October of 1991. You mentioned the name of Nikola Kalozi and his father. Before the conflict did you know this family?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you tell us how you knew them?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Before the 1990s, they had a restaurant in Erdut mountain, which was a part of the village of Erdut. We often went and dined there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court how you heard that Nikola Kalozi and his father were brought to the training centre?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: At that time the only way we could learn that was from other people's stories, as we were walking to work or as we were walking to the shops or the bakery. That's how I heard that they had been brought to the centre. I did not see them myself, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now you also mention in that same page the Albert family. Could you tell us what was your relationship, if any, to this family?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I don't know if my question was translated well. Could you tell us what was your relationship with this family?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I knew them. My sister was married to one of the Albert family members, and she still is, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And you mention in your statement that a man by the name of Milorad Stricevic was supposed to help the Albert family leave Erdut and cross into Serbia. Now, first of all, could you tell the Court who was Stricevic?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I didn't know Stricevic before 1990. In the 1990s I may have seen him once or twice. He was a friend of my brother-in-law -- or, rather, a friend of a friend of my brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did he -- what relations, if any, did he have with the Albert family?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: There were no family relations at all. They just knew each other through a mutual friend, through a friend of the Albert family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And after or following the month of August of 1991, did you know where he lived?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Stricevic lived in my sister's house and my brother-in-law's house in Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now in your statement you say that you realised that the Albert family, that is Djuro, Helena, and Victoria, and Ana Terzic had gone missing some two weeks later. Could you tell the Court how you learned that they went missing?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: How they disappeared, is that what you're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. How you learned that they disappeared.

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Before they left they came to say goodbye to my parents. They said to them that they would first go to Serbia, and from there that they would go to Hungary and then perhaps somewhere else. Perhaps ten days or so later, we got in touch with my sister and my brother-in-law through our friends in Odzak [as interpreted]. The telephone lines were down at that time. Those people from Odzak called my sister and my brother-in-law, who were in Slovenia at the time, and they heard from them that they had never contacted them. And based on that, some five or six days later, when they failed to get in touch, we concluded that they had gone missing, that they had left no traces. They had simply gone missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'd like to clarify something you mentioned about friends. And what's recorded in the transcript is the town of Odzak. Is that the right name of the town?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Odzaci. Odzak is a place in Bosnia and Odzaci is in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Now in that same paragraph, after you've talked about the Albert family and the case of Manda Maj, you say that some other Croats were put on buses and expelled from Erdut before UNPROFOR arrived. What I would like to ask you is which time-period would this be approximately?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: That expulsion I believe happened in spring.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And how did you learn about this expulsion?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: We heard about all of those important things on the street. I heard about that from my cousin. Arkan's men came and forced him at gunpoint to drive the bus with those Croats, i.e., non-Serbs from the village who were being expelled from the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what happened to the homes of the Croats who had been expelled?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Those houses were then rented out to the Serbian refugees who had arrived either from Osijek or from Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Were any Croats left after these expulsions in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Very few and they were mostly elderly or they were in mixed marriages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now you just told us that the Serb refugees who had been expelled from Osijek or Western Slavonia came to occupy some of the homes that were left behind by the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I would like to look at the following document, which is 65 ter 00982, and that is at tab 18. I don't know why the English version is in green.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is also a version in my language.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now the document describes the -- deals with the home owned by Drago Albert. Did you know Drago Albert?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Drago Albert is my sister's husband. He is my brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And what ethnicity is he?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Drago Albert, he was of Catholic faith.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: At the time, did you know that this house was given to the Vujanic family as indicated on this document?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we knew that. I knew it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And did you know where the Vujanic family came from?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I believe that they came from Podravska Slatina, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what was that you are ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Vujanic was of Orthodox faith.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: May I ask for this document to be admitted, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P275. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And I'm sorry, can we scroll down to the bottom of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature on this document, Ms. Rakic?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And who's signature is it?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: My husband's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you explained that at the time he was working for the Erdut local commune; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. He did work for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now the last document I'd like to show you is at 65 ter 00850.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's at tab 17. Now in the English version could we go to page 2, and in the B/C/S version could we go to page 5. Your Honours, this is a series of approximately 30 notifications to inhabitants of the village of Erdut. We will use a few examples here and we've translated one or two of them, but the documents are always similar, they are always the same. It is simply the name of the inhabitant which changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now could you tell us, Ms. Rakic, what this document is about? What's the subject here?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: This document is not very legible, I must say. However, this is a notification to the Serbian refugees who arrived in Erdut in 1991 and occupied empty Croatian homes. That decision was issued by the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina for all those who temporarily resided in the territory of Erdut and their original places of residence had been liberated, that they should go back to their original places of residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This document here is addressed -- this decision is addressed to Zoran Stojilovic [phoen]. Is this somebody you were familiar with?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I knew him, well, just in passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And do you know where he went to?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I think that he moved to Serbia. Or to be more precise, he went to Vojvodina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Is that also your husband's signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page. I believe we may have another version that is a bit clearer. I mean the next page in the B/C/S. We can always leave the English version as is. Perhaps the next one in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Ms. Dragana -- well, on this one, Ms. Rakic, do you recognise the person who is being notified?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Sofija Alvadzic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And where was she from?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: She came from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, in B/C/S can we go to the next page?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this name?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: No, not this name here, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Again in B/C/S can we go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, the name here appears to be Garosac. Is this somebody you were familiar with?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I believe that she also moved away. She went to Vojvodina, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let's move to the next page in the B/C/S version. Let's move again to the next one in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: On all these documents we can see that it's the same format. Is that right, Ms. Rakic?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let's try one or two more and I'll wrap it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page in the B/C/S -- oh, no, to another one, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Is this also someone you were familiar with, Ms. Rakic?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we move perhaps to the page that ends with 772. That's three pages later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The name here is Nikola Grubisic. Is this someone you were familiar with?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And where did he go to?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: He's in Bogojevo. As you cross the Danube from Erdut, that would be the first place in Vojvodina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And let's try one last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The very next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It's the name Milan Panic. Is that somebody you were familiar with?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him. Even before the 1990s.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not going to show the rest. There is about 20 more. Could I ask for this set of documents to be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P276. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Rakic, all these documents which are signed here are done in accordance with a decision of the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. At the time were you aware as to who was your husband's superior?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know who his superior was. We never discussed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examination, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Ms. Rakic. My name is Zoran Zivanovic. I represent Goran Hadzic in this case. Ms. Rakic, in your statement on page 2 you stated, inter alia, in paragraph 1 or 2, a paragraph that starts with the words, "On the 20th of July, 1991 ..." I apologise. It will be page 3. Not page 2. I misspoke. I believe that you can see that on the screen as well. You stated that a majority of women with small children left Erdut on the 20th of July, 1991. First of all, tell me please on that occasion when a majority of women with small children left Erdut, as you stated, does that refer to the women of all ethnic groups or just one ethnic group? What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Those were women of both ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, both Serbs and non-Serbs, right?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, on the 20th of July 1991, Erdut was under the control of the Croatian authorities, right?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can see that at that time you also left Erdut, on or about that time, together with your small child. Could you please tell us why you left? What prompted all the women and children to leave, women and children of both ethnic groups? What, for example, prompted you to leave Erdut at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Well, at the time members of the ZNG were in Erdut, members of the reserve Croatian police force. Guards were mounted at night. Croats from Erdut stood guard. Fire was opened at night. The troops were deployed in Bogojevo and they opened fire on each other. So naturally we were all afraid. We were concerned about our children. And therefore we decided to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you say that when you returned on the 19th of August, the village was almost empty?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Similarly, you said that after the 1st of August a sort of work obligation was introduced in Erdut, and what I'm interested in is whether this obligation concerned all the inhabitants of Erdut or was it a particular kind of obligation that depended on one's ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: No, all those who remained in Erdut and were capable of doing work had the will to carry out duties and they had that task too, and that concerned everyone, the Serbs, the Hungarians, the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time was this a legally prescribed work obligation? Were the regulations such at the time? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I don't think there were any legal regulations that concerned that obligation at the time. I think it was just a matter of people volunteering.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I won't put any further questions to you about the legal situation, about the laws of Yugoslavia and whether they were valid at the time. With regard to your first meeting with Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, if I have understood you correctly you said that he entered your office, he calmly introduced himself. I am asking you about this because on page 7, line 9, I think it was translated a little different. You, in fact, say that he stood as ease and then calmly introduced himself. I think it has happened again. When you say "calmly," do you mean he was calm or do you mean that he adopted the military position of being at ease?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Well, when I first met him I had never spoken to him but he did seem to be acting like a gentleman, which surprised me at the time. When he adopted that position, it wasn't as if he was saluting me in a military fashion, but he stood there, he sort of bowed and said, This is my name. He introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We have resolved that issue now. When you spoke about Milorad Stricevic and the Albert family, I just wanted you to clarify something for us. You said that the Albert family at the beginning of 1992 disappeared, in fact, and I would like to know whether you know anything about Milorad Stricevic. Did he subsequently appear anywhere? Do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: He was also found in the well, together with the Albert family. He and the Albert family were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about refugees who had found accommodation in certain houses in Erdut, you said that those houses had been let to those refugees. This is how it's been translated. It's page 17, line 15. But did they have to pay rent or were they provided with necessary accommodation? Because these people were very poor. They didn't have any property.

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: They didn't have to pay any rent. Perhaps when the electricity bills arrived they would have to pay for the bills, but at that time there was no rent to pay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And there is one other matter. My friend from the Prosecution -- my learned friend from the Prosecution showed you a lot of documents that concerned information provided to the Serbian refugees in 1992 -- 18th of June, 1992. It was information according to which they were to return to their places because the conditions were such that they could return. They didn't have to remain in that territory. So these houses that had been let to them had been let to them on a temporary basis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to ask you about. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Thank you -- you're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Anything in redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. No questions to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Rakic, I have a brief question for you. When we had a look at Exhibit P275, P275, we saw a signature. It was Drago Albert's signature. I apologise, Ljubomir Rakic's signature. Ljubomir Rakic. And when we had a look at the following exhibit, P276, Ljubomir Rakic's signature appears on that exhibit again. The person who signed the first document was president of the Commission for the Protection of Refugees, and the person who signed the second document was the secretary of the Executive Council of the Erdut commune. Are we dealing with the same person or not?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: It's the same person. The secretary [Realtime transcript read in error "secret"] of the local commune and the president of the commission is the same person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This Commission for the Protection of Refugees is an organisation that was under the auspices of the commune then?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I wasn't really informed but I think that that commission was a particular commission. It had a special status.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a slight error in the transcript. Judge Mindua, in response to your question, on page 26, line 14, and I see that the answer was: "The secret of the local commune ..." I think the witness said: "The secretary of the local commune."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Quite right. It is "the secretary" in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Rakic, I have a follow-up question for you on that matter. So I understand that it was your husband who signed the assignment of Drago Albert's house to a Serb refugee, right?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Drago Albert being your brother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Was this something you, after it happened, you discussed with your husband? Was this something -- was this odd? At first sight, it looks odd that your own husband gives away your brother-in-law's house. Did you discuss that with your husband? Were there any -- I don't know. Did you consider it as normal? I mean, was that a normal thing to do? Was this normal in his line of work?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: I'll explain. My sister and brother-in-law, when the army arrived they left. They went to Slovenia and they lived in Slovenia for a certain period of time. Later they returned to Osijek. Since all the abandoned houses were being let out to Serbian refugees who had arrived from Osijek or from other areas from which they had been expelled, well, all these houses were in fact let out to these Serbian refugees. Since the house that belonged to my sister and brother-in-law was a new one and we wanted to preserve it as well as the furniture in that house, since we knew that it had to be let to some of the Serbs who had arrived in Erdut, we tried to let it to someone we knew or who was known. Mr. Vujanic, who came from Podravska Slatina, knew a relative of my sister or the father of Drago Albert because Vujanic worked in the agricultural enterprise in Podravska Slatina and Drago Albert's father worked in the agricultural enterprise in Erdut. So they had a business relationship, they knew each other, and with his blessing, with the blessing of Drago's father, the house was let to a person who was known. And this was done in order to maintain the house, prevent it from being damaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So by doing this you were more or less taking care of your brother-in-law's house?

utterances.speaker: GORANA RAKIC
utterances.text: That's correct. That's correct. Because Drago Albert's father and the husband of the late Victoria Albert was still in Erdut in 1992, I think. When this was done he was still in Erdut.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So, Ms. Rakic, this brings your testimony to an end. Thank you for coming to The Hague to assist the Tribunal with your testimony. You're now released as a witness. The usher will escort you out of the courtroom and we wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have no additional witnesses to call today. The next witness will be arriving this afternoon from the region. We've got a bit of a gap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I regret that but sometimes it's inevitable. I think we weren't entirely sure how things would go with one of the earlier witnesses this week. So we have three witnesses who are now in the process of arriving or who will begin arriving today, and on our own calendar we think that we are down for calling and hopefully completing three witnesses during Thursday and Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Anything else to be discussed or addressed? Nothing. Court adjourned. We will resume, then, Thursday at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of November, 2012, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.17 a.m.,
